record.original_question: Can one establish general fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for fractional operators with distributed lag, especially in models where memory effects and distributed lag are present simultaneously?

evidence.quote: Simultaneous presence of memory effects and distributed lag is important for economic models.
However, for fractional operators with distributed lag, which are proposed in [161] and used in [162, 163], [107, Ch.20-23], the fundamental theorems of FC have not been proved in general.
This is an important direction of future research in FC and its applications in economics and physics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider fractional operators with continuously distributed lag, defined as follows. For an absolutely integrable probability density M:[0,∞)→[0,∞) (the lag distribution) and a function f:[0,∞)→ℝ, define the integer-order operator with distributed lag

  (T_M f)(t) = ∫_0^t M(t−τ) f(τ) dτ,

and, for α>0, the fractional integral and fractional derivative with distributed lag as the compositions of T_M with the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral I^α and with the Riemann–Liouville (or Caputo) fractional derivative D^α, e.g.

  (I^α_M f)(t) = (T_M ∘ I^α f)(t),   (D^α_M f)(t) = (D^α ∘ T_M f)(t),

so that memory effects (captured by I^α, D^α) and distributed lag (captured by M) are simultaneously present.

Establish, in this general setting, analogs of the first and second fundamental theorems of calculus: namely, identify natural function classes 𝒳 and broad classes of admissible lag kernels M for which one has

 (i) (First FT) D^α_M I^α_M f = f for all f ∈ 𝒳;
 (ii) (Second FT) I^α_M D^α_M f = f − (boundary/initial-value terms expressible through M and f),

and prove these identities, characterizing the kernels M and the orders α for which such fundamental theorems hold.
artifact.status_search_result: Within the framework of General Fractional Calculus (Kochubei 2011; Luchko 2020 onward) based on Sonine kernel pairs, general first and second fundamental theorems have been proven, and these GFC operators include cases interpretable as derivatives/integrals with continuously distributed lag. Thus the problem is partially solved: fundamental theorems are available for broad Sonine-kernel classes, but a fully general treatment specifically for the composed fractional-plus-distributed-lag operators in the form posed has not been uniformly established.

status_evidence.title: Fractional Derivatives and the Fundamental Theorem of Fractional Calculus (Luchko)
status_evidence.snippet: General fractional analogs of the first and second fundamental theorems of fractional calculus are proved for GFC operators with Sonine kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Fundamental theorems of fractional calculus have been established in the general fractional calculus framework.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Dynamics (arXiv:2510.17806)
status_evidence.snippet: GFD/GFI with kernels that are standard probability density functions can be interpreted as integer-order derivatives and integrals with continuously distributed lag.
status_evidence.claim: Distributed-lag operators are subsumed by general fractional calculus in special cases where fundamental theorems hold.

status_evidence.title: Fractional and Integer Derivatives with Continuously Distributed Lag
status_evidence.snippet: Definitions of fractional derivatives/integrals with distributed lag, used in economic models with simultaneous memory and lag.
status_evidence.claim: The operators under consideration are explicitly defined but their general fundamental theorems were not derived there.
